entities.note: 5x5 colour-9 square with a colour-5 centre pixel at rows 8-12, cols 14-18 (top-left cell of the grey floor); occupies one 6x6 cell of a 6-px lattice (cells at rows 8+6j, cols 14+6i) and moves 6 px per press

none on the first frame; after ACTION5 the old body reappears at the start cell recoloured 2 (centre 5) and replays the moves that body made, one per successful player move; it presses the pad exactly like the player

grey walkable region: a 5-cell-wide top room rows 7-13 cols 13-43, the left corridor cols 13-19 running rows 7-56, a side lobe rows 19-25 cols 13-31, the bottom corridor rows 49-55 cols 13-49 and a 3x3-cell block rows 48-56 cols 42-50 around the goal bracket; the player's centre must land on grey
black background everywhere else (rows 0-62): not walkable, a move whose destination is black is refused
3x3 colour-8 pad at rows 9-11, cols 39-41 (lattice cell (4,0), 4 cells right of the start); standing on it (player or ghost) lights the wire and opens the door; stepping off closes it
1-px colour-8 line from the pad down col 40 (rows 12-39) and left along row 40 (cols 19-40) to the door: shows which door the pad controls; not walkable, not interactive

colour-8 bracket-shaped door filling the left corridor at rows 38-42, cols 14-18 (lattice cell (0,5)); while the pad is held it slides 6 px right to cols 20-24 (over 6 animation frames) leaving the corridor open; when the pad is released it slides back; a move into the closed door is refused and a door closing on the player's centre kills

hollow colour-9 bracket at rows 49-55, cols 43-49 (top and bottom bars 7 px, right bar 5 px, open on the left) with a single colour-9 dot at (52,46) in its centre; the player must stand inside it (rows 50-54, cols 44-48 = lattice cell (5,7))

top-left rewind indicators: 3x3 squares at rows 1-3, cols 1-3 (hollow colour 9 = active) and cols 5-7 (solid colour 1 = unused), with a 3x1 colour-9 marker at row 5 under the active one; each ACTION5 turns the active square hollow colour 2 and moves the marker right; 2 squares = one ghost may exist at a time
row 63: colour 9 = remaining time, colour 1 track revealed from the RIGHT 1 px per 2 actions (blocked moves and rewinds count); empty = game over

rules.note: up one cell if the destination cell is grey floor and not the closed door; costs half a timer pixel
a move onto black, off the floor or into the closed door is refused: nothing moves, the ghost does not advance, but the timer still ticks (same for ACTION2/3/4)

every SUCCESSFUL player move (any of ACTION1-4) makes each ghost perform its next recorded move in lockstep (the ghost's own direction, not the current key); a ghost whose list is exhausted stays put; a blocked ghost move is skipped

when a move puts the player or a ghost ON the pad the door slides 6 px right out of the corridor (open); the move that takes the last body off the pad slides it back 6 px left (closed) (same for ACTION2/3/4); a door closing on the player's centre = lose
rewind: all recorded moves are undone and a fresh player appears at the start cell (rows 8-12, cols 14-18) with an empty move list; the door closes if nobody holds the pad
the body that was rewound becomes a colour-2 ghost at the start that will replay its recorded moves one per player move
the active indicator square turns colour 2 (used) and the marker moves under the next square
the 2nd rewind (L1 has 2 indicator squares) deletes every ghost instead of adding one and the counter resets, so at most one ghost exists; the pad is then released
ACTION5 with no recorded moves changes nothing but still ticks the timer; ACTION6/7 are not offered and do nothing

goal.note: the player must stand centred inside the bracket (rows 50-54, cols 44-48); the only route is the left corridor through the door cell, and the door stays open only while something holds the pad, so: walk 4 right onto the pad, ACTION5 (ghost re-walks to the pad and holds it), 7 down, 5 right = 17 actions

budget.note: 64 px, 1 px per 2 actions of any kind; the engine actually ends the game on the 130th action
